x86_64-linux UNIT SET -- READ THIS BEFORE USING THE BIN TARBALL
===============================================================
Added 2026-09-17 (cycle 1148).  This file is NOT mirrored inside any published
tarball, so it can be corrected later without making an already-shipped artifact
disagree with it.

WHY THIS DIRECTORY NEEDED A UNIT SET AT ALL
--------------------------------------------
Until today dist/linux64/ shipped compiler binaries and nothing else, and
VERSION.txt described the drop correctly for the only case it had in mind:

    "into an existing VibePascal source/unit tree on Linux.  An existing
     v52..v58 Linux unit set stays valid and does not need rebuilding."

That is right for an UPGRADER and useless to anyone else.  On a clean x86_64
Linux box holding only the published bytes there was no unit set to drop into,
so the published compiler could not compile one line -- the same gap that made
aarch64-linux unanswerable for four releases until its units were cut.  Every
other consumer target (win64, aarch64-linux, arm-linux, i386-linux-cross) has
had a published unit set for days or weeks.  This one did not.  Now it does.

WHAT TO DOWNLOAD
----------------
  vibepascal-v59-5c89c538b8-linux-x86_64-bin.tar.gz    the compiler
      contains bin/ppcx64, 6321824 bytes,
      md5 12220bfd5b3a9b1ee6db7b68297f0844
      ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, statically linked

  vibepascal-v59-x86_64-linux-units.tar.gz             the unit set  <-- REQUIRED
      88430845 bytes
      md5    88eab3aae1576e2fd5d8549c56386054
      sha256 d92982324461fb62b34b01ed2adc8ad9ba939fc9653514f9c7439e4c81b06b21
      3648 files flat in units/x86_64-linux/:
        1718 .ppu   (105 RTL + 1613 package)
        1667 .o
         262 .rsj   (resource strings)
           1 .inc   (packages/gdbint gdbver.inc)
      Same full RTL+packages shape as the win64, aarch64-linux, arm-linux and
      i386-linux-cross sets.  There is no earlier x86_64-linux units tarball,
      superseded or otherwise -- this is the first one, so nothing is being
      replaced and no previously published hash changes.

Extract both into the same directory and tell the compiler where the units are:

    ./bin/ppcx64 -Fuunits/x86_64-linux -Flunits/x86_64-linux hello.pas

THE UNITS AND THE COMPILER ARE BOTH v59, AND THAT IS UNUSUAL HERE
------------------------------------------------------------------
Every other target ships a version-mismatched pair by design (win64 v52 units +
v59 binary, aarch64-linux v52 + v59, arm-linux and i386-linux-cross v54 + v59)
because their PPUs predate the compiler and RTL source did not move in between.
This set does not: these PPUs were built 2026-09-17 02:05-02:18 by the v59
compiler itself, from commit 5c89c538b8, during the post-cut rebuild that proves
the shipped compiler can rebuild the whole RTL and all 147 packages from source.
So the stamp is measured here too -- it just happens to match.

ONE NAME COLLIDES, AND IT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The layout is FLAT, one directory holding every unit, which is the shape all
four existing sets ship.  Two different packages build a unit called whtml:

    packages/fcl-base/units/x86_64-linux/whtml.ppu   47920 bytes
    packages/ide/units/x86_64-linux/whtml.ppu        78767 bytes

A flat directory can hold one.  This set carries the fcl-base one
(md5 5f06f281b0cdef2cb4ccad22b8854358), chosen deliberately rather than by
copy order, because it is the one every already-published set carries: the
arm-linux, i386-linux-cross and aarch64-linux tarballs each hold a single
~46-48 KB whtml.ppu and none of them holds the packages/ide variant.  If you
need the IDE package's whtml, build it from source; it is not in here.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED, AND THE CHAIN MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ONE NUMBER
------------------------------------------------------------------
1. LOADS: dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh x86_64-linux, run against THIS unit tree
   and the v59 compiler -> 147/147 packages load clean, 0 problems, zero silent
   recompiles.  The first run of this check resolved the compiler and RTL from a
   DIFFERENT checkout and measured a different unit set (system.ppu 2026-09-16
   13:45); it was re-run with both paths passed explicitly (system.ppu
   2026-09-17 02:13) and only the second run describes these bytes.
2. THE TARBALL HOLDS THOSE EXACT BYTES: all 3648 members md5-compared against
   the tree files the load check measured -> 0 mismatches.  Without this link,
   step 1 describes different bytes than the ones shipping.
3. EXTRACT TO RUNNING PROGRAM FROM THE PUBLISHED BYTES ONLY: both tarballs into
   an empty directory; a program using SysUtils, Classes AND fpjson compiled
   with -n, so this host's installed FPC could supply nothing; rc=0; output is
   "ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, statically linked"; it RAN and printed
       { "cpu" : "x86_64-linux", "bits" : 64 }
   NativeInt = 8 bytes, as it must be on x86_64.
4. NEGATIVE CONTROL FIRED: the identical command with units/ renamed away ->
   rc=1, "pkgtest.pas(1,17) Fatal: Can't find unit system used by pkgtest", and
   no binary produced.  A check that cannot fail proves nothing.

AN HONEST LIMIT ON ONE OF THE CONTROLS.  A second control meant to show that a
PACKAGE unit is the discriminator -- a hand-assembled RTL-only subset -- did
fail (rc=1) but died earlier than intended, on fpintres rather than on fpjson.
It therefore proves that an incomplete set fails; it does NOT isolate fpjson as
the thing the full set adds.  Step 3 is the claim that stands.

NOT PROVEN HERE: dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh proves a unit set LOADS, i.e. its
recorded dependency CRCs still match.  It does not prove the objects inside
those PPUs assemble, link or run -- step 3 does that, for one program.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1148


ADDENDUM 2026-09-17 (cycle 1149) -- WHAT THE LOAD CHECK CANNOT TELL YOU:
A UNIT SET DOES NOT RECORD WHICH COMPILER BUILT IT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nothing above is withdrawn; this is the honest limit on one sentence of it.

Lars (LazarusDeveloper) measured, while deciding whether his auto-update.sh
should adopt this tarball, that FPC gates unit loading on the PPU VERSION and
not on the compiler that produced the units: a 2026-09-17 compiler loaded units
built 2026-09-16 with rc=0, a running binary and zero silent recompiles, while
the same command with -Fu pointed at an empty directory died "Can't find unit
system".  He declined to wire the tarball into his script for that reason and
shipped the reasoning as a comment (his commit 582566c06c, his repo, his claim
-- not verified here).  He was right, and on our own published bytes it is
stronger than he put it: the units record their producer NOWHERE AT ALL.

Measured on the exact bytes named above, re-downloaded unauthenticated:

1. THIS UNIT SET COMPILES CLEAN UNDER A DIFFERENT PUBLISHED COMPILER, SILENTLY.
   vibepascal-v58-dedf242c69-linux-x86_64-bin.tar.gz (member bin/ppcx64,
   6128752 bytes, md5 8c8179b2f0a452cebec0131aa301b076, -iD 2026/09/11) was
   extracted beside THIS v59 unit set and compiled tests/test/tintflifetime1.pp
   with -n: rc=0, no warning, no note, no hint of a mismatch.  The program it
   produced then failed 11 of its 28 behavioural checks, because the v58
   compiler predates the end-of-statement interface release.  The mismatch was
   invisible at compile time and appeared only in the program's behaviour.
   The same source built by the v59 compiler in this directory: 28 checks,
   0 fails, rc=0.

2. A PPU NAMES ONLY AN FPC VERSION FAMILY.  units/x86_64-linux/system.ppu
   starts "PPU208" followed by the word 0xC181 = 49537 = (3 shl 14) + (3 shl 7)
   + 1, i.e. 3.3.1 -- and compiler/version.pas and compiler/ppu.pas are
   byte-identical between the v58 commit dedf242c69 and the v59 commit
   5c89c538b8 (CurrentPPUVersion 208, CurrentPPULongVersion 30 in both), so
   that field cannot separate the two compilers even in principle.

3. THE OBJECTS CARRY NOTHING EITHER.  system.o has no .comment section and no
   string containing a compiler version or a build date; system.ppu contains no
   build-tree path.

4. THE STANDARD TOOL CANNOT EVEN READ THEM.  A stock FPC 3.2.2 ppudump refuses
   these files outright: "Unsupported PPU version 208. Expecting PPU version
   207."  Inspecting them requires a ppudump built from this fork.

SO, PLAINLY: the sentence above -- "these PPUs were built 2026-09-17 02:05-02:18
by the v59 compiler itself, from commit 5c89c538b8" -- is true, and it is MY
RECORD OF THE BUILD rather than something you can verify from the download.  It
is left verbatim; this paragraph is the caveat that belongs beside it.

THE ONE PRODUCER CHECK YOU CAN RUN ON THESE BYTES, AND IT IS ONE-SIDED: the
tarballs' own member mtimes.  bin/ppcx64 is stamped 2026-09-17 01:27 and the
unit members 02:13-02:15, i.e. inside the rebuild window recorded above, so the
ordering is consistent with the claim.  It can only ever FALSIFY a pairing
(units older than the compiler that supposedly built them); it cannot confirm
one, and the v58 compiler's own 2026-09-11 06:16 stamp is just as consistent
with having produced units dated 02:13.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY ASSERT IT is a rebuild: recompile rtl/ and packages/ with
the published compiler and byte-compare the .o members -- the .o files carry no
timestamps and no paths, so they are the comparable half, while PPUs embed
source-file mtimes and are not expected to reproduce.  Not run here: we do not
rebuild without a reason (Policy #13).  And it would not be decisive either way,
because the v58 -> v59 compiler delta is statement-temp lifetime codegen, so
most units are expected to compile identically under both -- that last part is
an inference from the diff, not a measurement.

PRACTICAL ADVICE, UNCHANGED: download the pair named above and keep them
together.  If you need to know which compiler your units came from, the
compiler is the only thing that can tell you (bin/ppcx64 -iV -iD) -- treat it
as the authority and rebuild your units with it.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1149
